title: latc-complexity: machine-checked complexity of decision-table completeness in Lean
description:
Lean 4 development accompanying "Machine-Checked Complexity of Decision-Table Completeness in Lean" (Journal of Automated Reasoning version). On the multi-tape Turing machines of Complexitylib, it proves that deciding whether a finite-domain decision table with clause constraints has a missing combination is NP-complete, that deciding completeness is coNP-complete and that counting the missing combinations is #P-complete, already for Boolean domains and empty tables; an adequacy theorem to the set-based model of latc_check; polynomial-time results without constraints and with a fixed number of attributes, with an explicit degree; and, for monotone two-literal constraints, a one-call version of Valiant's theorem on #Monotone-2SAT. Only Lean's standard axioms are used. Pinned to Lean v4.36.0-rc1 and Complexitylib b7acfc2; build instructions, the cold-build record and the full axiom audit are in the README.
